name_en: Fukure gashi — baking-soda-leavened black-sugar cake, steamed until it puffs up
summary_ja: 小麦粉と重曹、黒糖を混ぜて蒸す郷土菓子で、重曹でふっくら膨らむことからソーダ菓子とも呼ばれる。薩摩藩が奄美・琉球の黒糖生産を独占した歴史を背景に、黒糖菓子として鹿児島に根づいた。
summary_en: Wheat flour, baking soda, and black sugar are mixed and steamed into a cake that puffs up from the soda, earning it the nickname soda-gashi. It took root in Kagoshima against the backdrop of the Satsuma domain's monopoly on Amami and Ryukyu black-sugar production.
source_title: ふくれ菓子 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Shirokuma — shaved ice under condensed milk, ringed with fruit and red bean
summary_ja: 削り氷に練乳をかけ、チェリーやみかん、小豆を色とりどりにのせた鹿児島発祥の氷菓。上から見た姿が白熊に似ることからこの名がついたと伝わり、夏の鹿児島を象徴する一品として親しまれている。
summary_en: Shaved ice under condensed milk, ringed with cherries, mandarin, and red bean in bright color. The name is said to come from how the toppings look, seen from above, like a polar bear's face — and it's become a summer emblem of Kagoshima.
source_title: 白熊 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Kasha mochi — mugwort mochi wrapped in a broad, fragrant leaf and steamed
summary_ja: よもぎとさつまいも、黒糖を練った餅を、殺菌効果があるとされるクマタケランの葉で包んで蒸す奄美地域の菓子。葉の芳香が餅に移り、身近な素材だけでつくる先人の知恵が詰まっている。
summary_en: Mugwort, sweet potato, and black sugar are kneaded into mochi and wrapped in a broad-leafed ginger-family plant said to have antibacterial properties, then steamed. The leaf's scent seeps into the mochi — a sweet built entirely from what Amami had close at hand.
source_title: かしゃもち 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Getanha — a triangular black-sugar cake, its surface dipped glossy in syrup
summary_ja: 小麦粉と重曹の生地を黒糖で焼き、三角に切って黒糖蜜にくぐらせる菓子。米の集荷地だった横川町で客をもてなすお茶うけとして生まれ、泥に汚れた下駄の歯に見た目が似ることからこの名がついたと伝わる。
summary_en: A wheat-and-soda dough baked with black sugar, cut into triangles, and dipped glossy in black-sugar syrup. It's said to have begun as a teatime treat for visitors to Yokogawa, once a rice-collection town, its name likening the shape to a mud-caked wooden clog's teeth.
source_title: げたんは 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Karukan — a featherlight steamed cake of grated mountain yam, once served only to lords
summary_ja: すりおろした自然薯とかるかん粉を蒸し上げる、蒸す前より軽くなることから「軽羹」と書かれる鹿児島の銘菓。薩摩藩主が江戸から招いた菓子職人が考案したと伝わり、当初は大名家だけの菓子だった。
summary_en: Grated mountain yam and rice flour are steamed into a cake so light it's named with characters meaning 'light yokan' — steaming leaves it lighter than the raw batter. Said to have been devised by a confectioner the Satsuma lord brought from Edo, it was once a treat reserved for the ruling family alone.
source_title: かるかん 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Karaimo nettabo — freshly pounded mochi kneaded with steamed sweet potato
summary_ja: つきたての餅に蒸したさつまいもを練りこみ、きなこと砂糖をまぶして食べる鹿児島の餅菓子。台風に強く痩せた土地でも育つさつまいもが根づいた歴史を背景に、年末年始の餅つきに欠かせない一品となった。
summary_en: Freshly pounded mochi is kneaded together with steamed sweet potato, then dusted with soy flour and sugar. It grew out of sweet potato's deep roots here — a crop that shrugs off typhoons and thin soil — and became a fixture of year-end mochi-pounding.
source_title: からいもねったぼ 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Janbo mochi — two skewers through soft mochi, glazed in a thick soy-sugar sauce
summary_ja: つきたての餅に竹串を2本刺し、とろみのある砂糖醤油ダレをかける鹿児島市磯地域の郷土菓子。南北朝時代、谷山城で懐良親王をもてなした逸話に由来すると伝わり、「両棒」と書いて「じゃんぼ」と読む。
summary_en: Fresh mochi threaded on two bamboo skewers, glazed with a thick soy-and-sugar sauce — a specialty of Kagoshima City's Iso district. Its name, written with characters for 'two poles,' is said to trace to an episode of hospitality shown to a visiting prince at Taniyama Castle in the fourteenth century.
source_title: じゃんぼ餅 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Akumaki — mochi rice steeped in wood-ash lye, wrapped in bamboo sheath, boiled for hours
summary_ja: 灰汁に浸したもち米を孟宗竹の皮で包み、灰汁水で数時間煮こむ端午の節句の餅菓子。西郷隆盛も戦陣食として食べたと伝わり、灰汁のアルカリ性が雑菌の繁殖を抑え、高温多湿の鹿児島で長期保存を可能にした。
summary_en: Mochi rice steeped in wood-ash lye is wrapped in bamboo sheath and boiled for hours in more lye water — a Boys' Festival sweet said to have fed Saigo Takamori's troops in the field. The lye's alkalinity holds bacteria back, letting it keep for days in Kagoshima's heat and humidity.
source_title: あくまき 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理
